args.new:
if whole_number:
        return f"{whole_number} {abs(numerator):.0f}/{denominator:.0f}"

    # int() truncates toward zero, so for a negative number the numerator
    # carries the minus sign, which prints as "-3/10". The sign already rides
    # on the whole part (which is 0 here); absorb it from the fractional part
    # so the result reads as a normal fraction.
    return f"{abs(numerator):.0f}/{denominator:.0f}"

# Test positive mixed fractions

assert humanize.fractional(-2.75) == '-2 3/4', f'-2.75 failed: {humanize.fractional(-2.75)}'
assert humanize.fractional(-1.5) == '-1 1/2', f'-1.5 failed: {humanize.fractional(-1.5)}'
# Test pure fractions (no whole part)
assert humanize.fractional(0.3) == '3/10', f'0.3 failed: {humanize.fractional(0.3)}'
assert humanize.fractional(0.5) == '1/2', f'0.5 failed: {humanize.fractional(0.5)}'
assert humanize.fractional(float(1/3)) == '1/3', f'1/3 failed: {humanize.fractional(float(1/3))}'
# Test integers
assert humanize.fractional(1) == '1', f'1 failed: {humanize.fractional(1)}'
assert humanize.fractional(0) == '0', f'0 failed: {humanize.fractional(0)}'

"
